obligation: CISA report under the rail cybersecurity directive
trigger: Cybersecurity incident involving IT or OT systems a Covered Railroad operates or maintains (unauthorized access, malware, denial of service, or potential operational disruption)
deadline: As soon as practicable and no later than 72 hours after identification; group target 24 hours so the report also satisfies 49 CFR 1570.203 (II.C.5)
notifying_entity: Group CISO as primary Cybersecurity Coordinator, for each affected Covered Railroad
clock_starts: When the owner/operator identifies the cybersecurity incident

trigger: Required report fields not available at the first report
deadline: Within 24 hours of the information becoming available

obligation: TSA report of a significant security concern (cyber attack)
trigger: Cyber attack on any railroad, including the 58 not covered by the directives
deadline: Within 24 hours of initial discovery; for Covered Railroads, met by the CISA report if it states it is made under the directive
notify: TSA by the method TSA prescribes (TSOC telephone 1-866-655-7023)
notifying_entity: Vice President, Rail Security (primary TSA Security Coordinator)

obligation: TSOC call recommended by TSA information circular
trigger: Actual or potential significant cybersecurity incident
deadline: As soon as possible and no more than 12 hours after discovery (recommendation, not a requirement)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes: adopted by group policy for all railroads (POL-03 4.4)

trigger: SSI (for example the CIP or CAP results) released to unauthorized persons, including theft by the attacker
deadline: Promptly
clock_starts: When the group becomes aware of the release

obligation: Answer TSA requests for RSSM car locations during the outage
trigger: TSA requests location and shipping information while the TMS or NOC systems are down
deadline: Within 30 minutes of the request (not Class I)
notifying_entity: NOC on-duty manager using the printed list and offline extract

obligation: CIP amendment after a permanent change
trigger: Recovery changes Critical Cyber Systems or measures for 45 days or more (for example a rebuilt PTC back office or removal of the directory trust)
deadline: Within 50 days after the permanent change takes effect
clock_starts: When the permanent change takes effect

obligation: FRA telephonic report of an accident or incident
trigger: Only if the cyber event leads to an accident or incident of the kinds 225.9 lists
deadline: Immediately, as 225.9 specifies
applies_at_this_tier: Assess: not triggered by a cyber event alone (C-TRANSPORTATION-S05)
clock_starts: Occurrence of the accident or incident

obligation: PTC safety-relevant failure notice to FRA and the vendor
trigger: Only if the PTC system shows a safety-relevant failure or defective condition above the PTCSP thresholds or not previously identified
deadline: Within 15 days after discovery of the failure
applies_at_this_tier: Assess with the PTC vendor: CR-11 to CR-14 (C-TRANSPORTATION-S04)
clock_starts: Discovery of the failure, malfunction, or defective condition

trigger: Only if a hazmat incident listed in 171.15(b) occurs during transportation (for example a release with injury or a closure of a major artery for 1 hour or more)
deadline: As soon as practical and no later than 12 hours after the occurrence
applies_at_this_tier: Assess: railroads and Transload and Wholesale (C-TRANSPORTATION-S06)
notifying_entity: Hazmat compliance manager of the division in possession

obligation: Operational notice to passenger operators and Class I hosts
citation: Operating, interoperability, and trackage rights agreements
trigger: Dispatch or PTC back office degraded on host territory or tenant runs
deadline: Immediately by the NOC; written notice as each agreement requires
notify: Amtrak; commuter operator; Class I railroads
applies_at_this_tier: Yes: CR-11 to CR-14 and 24 tenant railroads
clock_starts: Decision to go to manual dispatch or PTC failure procedures

trigger: Incident affecting dispatch or car management for a CDS customer
deadline: Within 24 hours of identification

trigger: The disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination; determination without unreasonable delay

trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents (employees, drivers)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred; 15 more days only with good cause given to the Department in writing within the 30 days
notifying_entity: The employing subsidiary, through the Group General Counsel
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (no extension for this notice)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the covered entity
trigger: A vendor or corporate service that maintains personal information for a subsidiary has a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days after determining the breach
notify: The subsidiary that owns the data
applies_at_this_tier: Yes: corporate shared services and SaaS vendors (C-TRANSPORTATION-S07)
notifying_entity: Group General Counsel (for corporate); the vendor (for vendors)

citation: Each state where affected individuals reside
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents of any of the 28 states
deadline: Per each state law; plan to the shortest clock among affected states
notify: Affected residents; state attorneys general where required
notifying_entity: Group General Counsel with outside breach counsel

trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services identified in a system during response
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification, then mitigation details within 10 business days
notify: Contracting Officer of each of the 7 federal contracts

trigger: A Kaspersky covered article identified during response
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification, then mitigation details within 10 business days
notify: Contracting Officer of each of the 7 federal contracts

trigger: FCI exposure
deadline: No reporting duty in the clause; inform contracting officers if FCI is involved, as the contracts compliance manager judges appropriate

trigger: Building access control, life safety monitoring, or tenant data affected
deadline: As each lease requires
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Real Estate systems are affected

trigger: Any Severity 1 incident
deadline: As the policy requires; group practice is the same day

trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As soon as practical; supports the OFAC mitigation factors if payment is ever considered

obligation: Voluntary CISA report for non-rail divisions
trigger: Incident in Transload and Wholesale or Real Estate systems not covered by the directive
deadline: As soon as practical

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
trigger: Any consideration of a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment
notify: OFAC (if a license is needed); law enforcement

obligation: CIRCIA covered incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: 72 hours and 24 hours as proposed; not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (C-TRANSPORTATION-R07)
clock_starts: Not applicable until a final rule is effective

trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers
deadline: No later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No: no division is a financial institution with consumer customers (N53-R01)

trigger: Incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No: no DoD contracts or CUI (N42-R03)
